A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 26-page versions of Adversarial Flow Models. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-I support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original Gaussian-mixture simulations and ImageNet-256 generation experiments, including hyperparameter ablations, depth comparisons, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original simulations and ImageNet experiments, with quantitative results and qualitative analyses in both the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1-3 retain the same adversarial and optimal-transport objectives, gradient normalization, guidance procedures, architectures, and training steps.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian-mixture scenarios and class-conditional ImageNet-256 generation coverage, including guided, unguided, single-step, and multi-step settings.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons in Tables 4-6 and 9 and Figure 9 retain the same comparator sets, including MeanFlow, AlphaFlow, TiM, GAN baselines, and SiT. Updated citation years refer to the same methods.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix D retain the same preprocessing, latent representation, model configurations, training schedules, and evaluation procedures. Both evaluate 50,000 class-balanced samples, with 50 samples per ImageNet class.

E4.justification: The optimal-transport and gradient-penalty ablations, guidance tests, depth comparisons, latent interpolation, layer visualizations, and gradient-normalization analyses are retained without substantive revision.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains its average-of-two-runs reporting and labeled variation. The seed descriptions and other uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged; no new statistical estimation procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Result entries and findings are unchanged. For example, Tables 4 and 7 retain FIDs of 2.38 for XL/2 single-step generation and 2.08/1.94 for the 56/112-layer models. Appendix image recompression preserves the same displayed samples.

T1.justification: The optimal-transport assumptions and reasoning, guidance derivations in Appendix F, and discrete-flow formulation in Appendix H are unchanged. No mathematical definition, equation, or proof is substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about deterministic transport, training stability, preserved model capacity, generation performance, and end-to-end training of deep single-step models.

C2.justification: Interpretations of generalization, guidance, and depth scaling remain unchanged. Section 4.4 and the appendices retain the same computational, memory, gradient-vanishing, evaluation-comparability, and applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: Implementation listings, hyperparameters, precision, training schedules, and code/VAE access information are retained. The added acknowledgement of GPU support supplies no hardware specification or new reproduction instructions.

R1.justification: Matching preprints to their publication entries establishes the same cited works and research positioning. Changes to venues, years, titles, and author metadata do not add research connections or revise novelty claims.

P1.justification: v3 adds an ICML proceedings/copyright notice and acknowledges Xu Hu for GPU access. It updates bibliographic metadata and corresponding citations, including Adam's author attribution. The scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain intact.

P2.justification: The proceedings notice and expanded bibliography cause limited text reflow. Figures 5-8 retain the same sample grids and dimensions with stronger JPEG compression. Figure and table organization remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 mainly updates publication metadata and acknowledgements while preserving the scientific argument, experimental evidence, derivations, reproducibility information, and limitations. The bibliography is more complete, while appendix sample grids undergo stronger compression without changing their visible findings. These limited presentation changes produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
